correctness.rationale: For z(t)=t+i t² the two quadratic deck involutions are t↦i−t and t↦−i−t after coefficient conjugation. A rational modulus quotient invariant under both must be 2i-periodic and hence constant. For degree≤n, every squared-magnitude difference has real-parameter degree≤4n, yielding 4n+1 sufficiency. For n≥1, the positive rational modulus ratios Φ_n(u) built from imaginary-axis roots have exactly 2n strictly positive sign crossings: the base has two; each induction step preserves previous sign witnesses and creates two extra crossings, while the numerator difference has degree≤2n+2, proving exactness. Each u gives ±√u, yielding 4n actual distinct parabola samples at which non-phase-equivalent degree-n polynomials agree. The construction has nonvanishing denominators and asymptotic ratio>1. The dependency-free exact rational checker replays degrees 1–4; this finite verification is supplemental.

originality.rationale: The accepted statement is the complete worst-case sample-count theorem on one nondegenerate parabola, including its sharp all-degree lower construction, rather than merely the familiar reflection trick. Examination of Chalendar–Partington (arXiv:2403.16255), Liehr (arXiv:2308.05722) and Orevkov–Pakovich (arXiv:2309.04983), and targeted literature and mathematical-record queries, yielded no stated theorem giving the sharp 4n+1 sample threshold or a construction of 4n magnitude coincidences on this prescribed parabola in every degree. Ellipse/hyperbola and parallel-line results are distinct and do not imply the sharpness assertion. Priority is provisional, with the residual risks recorded.
residual_risks: A broader theorem about real intersections of generalized rational lemniscates with prescribed nonsingular conics may imply some or all of the all-degree sharpness claim indirectly.
Older or poorly indexed results on minimum numbers of phaseless polynomial samples along algebraic curves may contain an equivalent sharp sample threshold.
No independent historical-priority assessment was performed; failure to find an equivalent is not proof of global novelty.

value.rationale: The exact universal measurement threshold is a natural design invariant for degree-bounded complex polynomial phase retrieval along a single curved observation aperture. The 4n+1 upper bound alone is an elementary zero count, but its exact all-degree necessity is not: a recursive rational-lemniscate crossing construction uses controlled roots at successively remote imaginary locations to force 4n distinct real coincidences while preserving the previous ones. The theorem also gives a structural rigidity mechanism via noncommuting polynomial deck involutions. It is an infinite-dimensional-degree family with exact worst-case measurement complexity, not an arbitrary numerical slice, generic-count claim or rehash of fixed-grid tabulations.
